claim: For every finite field \(k=\mathbb F_q\), the centralizer Lie algebras \(C_{\mathfrak n_4(k)}(X)\) of elements of the six-dimensional strictly upper-triangular \(4\times4\) Lie algebra have precisely five isomorphism types when \(q\) is even and six when \(q\) is odd. The types and multiplicities are: the full \(\mathfrak n_4\), count \(q\); the five-dimensional two-step Lie algebra \(\mathfrak s_5\) with brackets \([t,u]=z_1,[t,v]=z_2\), count \(q(q^2-1)\) in even characteristic and \(2q(q-1)\) in odd characteristic; the five-dimensional class-three algebra \(\mathfrak f_4\oplus k\), count zero in even characteristic and \(q(q-1)^2\) in odd characteristic; \(\mathfrak h_3\oplus k\), count \(q^3(q^2-1)\); abelian \(k^4\), count \(q^3(q-1)\); and abelian \(k^3\), count \(q^3(q-1)(q^2-1)\). In particular the class-three five-dimensional centralizer type occurs exactly when \(\operatorname{char}k\ne2\).

correctness.rationale: The three exact commutator coordinates are solved in all disjoint cases d!=0, d=0 and (a,f)!=0, and d=a=f=0. Explicit bases and all internal Lie brackets establish each abstract type, including the -2be coefficient that detects characteristic two. The six counts sum to q^6. Standalone independent exact-nullspace and lower-central calculations exhaust F2,F3,F4,F5 and match the symbolic formulas; the proof covers all finite fields.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of a natural family of element centralizer Lie algebras in the smallest non-Heisenberg unitriangular nilradical. The genuine sharp characteristic-two disappearance of class-three centralizers and explicit same-adjoint-rank nonisomorphism witnesses refine existing centralizer-dimension, commuting-pair and rank statistics, supplying a reusable small-rank model for centralizer geometry.
